answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance comes from costly identity: every agent posts an onyx-signed stake that is slashed whenever its umber ledger of peer attestations conflicts with the network. A single operator can spawn many copies, but each copy must carry its own locked stake and build its own honest history before it earns an opal ranking or a vote. Attack cost then scales linearly with identities while honest capital stays pooled, so buying enough fake agents to out-vote the network costs more than it can extract.
